findings.action: Complete transferred-member acceptance at the canonical destination. ArtifactResolver deliberately retains the original Identity while returning the destination's CanonicalIdentity, Revision and Digest (artifact_ref.go:250-268; verified by TestArtifactGraphTransferMetadataPreservesIdentityAndProofs). federatedAcceptance selects resolved.Identity, opens that original project's store, and verifies the destination revision/digest against the original artifact at line 439. A cross-project transfer therefore produces source-revision-unavailable or source-artifact-uncommitted instead of accepting the authorized terminal destination. CloseoutMemberTarget fixes the child lookup, but both CLI roadmapGate and terminal closeout still run this acceptance path over the original member reference. Use canonical identity consistently for destination proof, revisions and trust while preserving authorization of the redirect chain. The round-six test checks that the source stub is not a child blocker; it does not establish successful composed acceptance.

Doctor must retain the applicable receipt/review obligation after terminal verification fails. CloseoutReviewsOwed first finds closedByReceipt false, but then computes currentCloseoutDecision and skips the scope whenever its current threshold says review is unnecessary. A scope closed under always whose review is later rejected, followed by an authorized switch to never, is omitted even though closeoutReviewGate preserves its required receipt decision and closeout-check rejects it. The same omission occurs for a voluntary review rejected after a never receipt. Use the applicable gate and recorded-review verification rather than the current threshold alone; historical no-receipt scopes already have separate handling.

Apply the adopted aggregate terminal gate to dependent-spec readiness and local spec dependency acceptance. SpecReadinessWithResolver considers a resolved dependency satisfied solely when Status is done. ArtifactResolver derives a milestone's done status from its members, so a draft spec depending on a reached milestone becomes ready before its mandatory explicit close and receipt, including under always with no aggregate approval. A done roadmap with pending closeout intent is similarly accepted by status. FederatedSpecAcceptance also explicitly skips unqualified and same-project dependencies at federated_acceptance.go:327, so the new localScopeClosed check inside aggregate acceptance does not repair this consumer. Resolve applicable aggregate terminal closeout cycle-safely before satisfying these dependencies, preserving legacy contracts. This violates the spec's explicit requirement that dependent readiness require the new close receipt.

Do not discard done roadmaps before checking adopted milestone terminal standing. ReachedMilestones and milestoneReachedObligations obtain candidates through milestonesWithTerminalMembers, which unconditionally skips every done roadmap. After a newly adopted roadmap and its milestones close with receipts, a later rejected member review or invalidated dependency makes their terminal closeout fail, but their milestones never reach the new closedByReceipt filter and disappear from reached/attention obligations. Enumerate these receipt-governed scopes and suppress them only when the applicable terminal projection stands. Preserve the explicitly exempt legacy roadmap contract.
